text.aura: Your aura is a wildflower growing through a crack in the pavement: lovely, adaptable and much tougher than it looks. Eul has a soft, approachable glow that makes people want to talk to you. You read as friendly, creative and easy to be around, the person strangers ask to take their photo because you look like you'd make them look good. There's movement in your energy, a lightness that changes shape depending on the room. That's your gift and your challenge. Your glow is at its brightest when it's clearly yours, not borrowed from whoever you're with. The glow-up for you is deepening the color of that flower, so people remember not just that you were lovely, but exactly who you were.
text.how-people-read-you: First impression: sweet, warm, maybe a little younger than you are. People feel comfortable around you almost instantly, and they often tell you things they didn't plan to share. The risk is being underestimated. Some people read your gentleness as softness, then are surprised when you quietly get exactly what you wanted. Others think you agree with everyone, because you're so good at seeing all sides. What people miss is how resilient you are. Vines survive storms that snap trees. To be read more accurately, let your opinions show early. Disagree once in a conversation, kindly. Wear something that signals taste, not just niceness. You don't need to lose your warmth to be taken seriously. You just need a few more clear lines in the picture.
text.colors: Your home palette is soft Wood: sage, mint, pistachio, leafy green, a little olive. These look effortless on you, like you stepped out of a garden café. Water supports you, so soft blues, denim and misty gray work well as base colors. For charm and visibility, add a touch of Fire: blush, peach, soft coral, petal pink. That combination, green with a little pink, is pure flower energy and looks wonderful in photos. You can wear florals and prints better than most souls, especially small, delicate ones. Avoid looking washed out in head-to-toe beige or harsh, heavy black without a soft accent. You do best in colors that look alive, like they're still growing.
text.style: Your style is soft romantic with an artsy edge. Flowy midi skirts, cardigans, oversized shirts, ribbon details, little jewelry pieces you collect over time. You look great in layers and textures, especially when they move as you walk. Mixing vintage finds with simple basics feels very you. The trap is wearing whatever your friends or partner like, until your closet looks like five different people. Choose a signature: maybe it's always a hair clip, a particular perfume, a silver ring stack, a certain shade of green. One consistent detail makes your style recognizable without losing flexibility. Hair with gentle texture or a soft accessory suits your movement. Your best photo spot is somewhere with flowers, plants or soft window light, mid-laugh, slightly turned.
text.vibe: The vibe to aim for is soft but certain. Picture a webtoon heroine who seems sweet in chapter one and turns out to be the most quietly unstoppable person in the story. The shift for you is self-definition. Say what you like, out loud, often. Order first at dinner. Keep your style choices even when someone teases them. Small acts like this make your aura go from pretty to unforgettable. Also try making things: arranging flowers, styling a shelf, curating a playlist for no one in particular. Your creativity shows on you. Keep your gentleness, it's genuinely magnetic. Just let people feel the stem beneath the petals, the part of you that keeps growing no matter what gets in the way.
text.aura-dims: Your aura dims when you've been bending for too long. You start to look tired from people-pleasing: the smile is still there, but it's on autopilot. Your style gets vague too, borrowed outfits, safe neutrals, nothing that says you. That's the sign you've been living around other people's preferences. The reset is reclaiming your space. Spend an afternoon alone doing exactly what you want, no compromise. Wear your favorite color even if it doesn't match anything. Rearrange your room, buy yourself flowers, play the music you secretly love. Text one friend who makes you laugh without needing anything from you. Vines are strongest when they're reaching toward light they've chosen, not just clinging to the nearest wall.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, your aura is a wildflower. Soft, friendly, strangers instantly trust you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also assume you'll agree with whatever they say. Do you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sage green and blush pink on you look like a garden café poster.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your closet has five different personalities. Pick yours.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is soft but certain. Same sweetness, clearer opinions.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One signature detail. Then stop borrowing your best friend's whole vibe.

spring.intro: Spring is home turf for Eul, so your aura is the vine in full flower: fresh, sociable, easy to like. People read you as friendly and stylish without effort, the one whose outfit gets asked about at brunch. The danger of being in season is excess. You can pile on prints, florals, charms and trends until the flower is lost in the hedge. Your glow-up is editing. Metal, the element that controls Wood, brings a frame: one silver chain, a white tee under a floral, a tidy bag with structure. Keep florals, they are your birthright, but wear one at a time. Spring Eul at its best looks like a single branch of blossom in a clean glass vase.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Eul, a floral dress, floral bag and floral clip is a garden center. Pick one.

summer.intro: Summer heat draws on Wood to keep Fire burning, so a summer Eul aura is a flower in bright sun: open, colorful, warm, and occasionally drooping by evening. People read you as fun, chatty and photogenic, and you probably own more coral and pink than anyone you know. Because your element is being spent, your look can turn scattered on tired days, one bright thing thrown on top of another. Water is your resource, so cool it down with ocean blues, deep teal and one crisp navy piece. Keep a single bright accent, a pink bag or a pair of loud earrings, so your sunshine stays. The summer Eul glow-up looks like a garden just after evening rain.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Eul, keep the pink bag. Swap the rest for ocean blue. Instant evening-garden energy.

autumn.intro: Autumn's Metal prunes Wood, so an autumn Eul aura is soft but watchful, a flower that learned to grow between rocks. People read you as gentle, polished and slightly reserved, and you often dress to avoid being criticized: neutral, safe, tidy, nothing anyone could comment on. Your glow-up is letting your softness be visible on purpose. Water, which feeds Wood and calms Metal, gives you dusky blues and inky florals. Add one botanical detail that is unmistakably yours: a leaf brooch, an embroidered collar, a green ring you never take off. You do not need to blend into the stone. The flower growing out of the wall is the thing everyone stops to photograph.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Eul, dressing so nobody can criticize you also means nobody remembers you. Wear the brooch.

winter.intro: Winter Water nourishes Wood, but frost keeps flowers closed, so a winter Eul aura is quiet, refined and a little hidden. People read you as mysterious or shy before they discover how funny you are. Your wardrobe leans dark and cozy, which suits the season, but it hides your bloom under three layers of charcoal. Your glow-up is sunlight. Fire is the warmth a winter vine waits for, so add blush, apricot, warm pink or a soft red knit. Keep greens for accessories so your Wood stays present. A winter Eul looks best like a camellia in snow: one warm flower against deep colors, impossible to ignore and lovely to stand next to.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Eul, an apricot knit under that charcoal coat. A camellia in the snow.

earth.intro: Earth days end each season, and an Eul Wood born in them carries the aura of a vine over warm ground: approachable, adaptable and easy to underestimate. People feel comfortable with you right away. Your style might blend in a little too well. Your glow-up is a stronger line. Wood needs Water to grow, so add soft navy or deep teal, and let one piece of fresh green or a floral print be the thing people remember. A vine is most striking in bloom. Pick one detail that says you, not the room.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Eul, stop matching the room. Wear the one thing the room doesn't have.

strength.strong: A strong Eul Wood aura is a climbing rose that has taken over the whole fence. With plenty of Wood and Water support, you are stylish, adaptable and endlessly creative, and you can't resist adding one more charm, one more print, one more trend from last week. The blind spot is overwhelming the eye. Your look becomes so busy that people remember the outfit more than you. Edit with Metal: a clean white or silver anchor, fewer pieces, a single focal point per look. Your taste is genuinely excellent. It looks even better with some breathing room around it.
strength.weak: A weak Eul Wood aura is a shy sprout growing in someone else's shadow. With little Wood or Water support, you tend to mirror whoever is around: their palette, their brands, their idea of what looks good. The blind spot is disappearing into other people's taste until you cannot say what yours is. Your glow-up is claiming a signature: one recurring botanical motif, one green you love, one fabric that feels like you. Wear it until people associate it with your name and buy you things in it. Your style doesn't have to be loud. It just needs to be unmistakably yours.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
